items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And I loved a date where I could be creative a little bit and on Burt’s dates too, I used to do these classical guitar fills that he liked a lot.

ctx.x: What were some of the pop acts that you might have played in the studio with?

Well I guess Burt Bachrach. I would consider him pop music. I mean it was good music in its own way. And he used to really get carried away with whatever little thing I did. “Oh man, you hear what he did there — bing!” Or something like that. And I loved it. And of course it was nice to be appreciated. And I loved a date where I could be creative a little bit and on Burt’s dates too, I used to do these classical guitar fills that he liked a lot. And I liked when I had a line to play though, mostly. If it was a…
Did you happen to play on an album with Jackie & Roy called “Time and Love?” Does that ring a bell with you? It was a CTI thing I think.
